LESSON: A fixture that lives in TWO repos is a stronger control than one whose second copy is a test in the same repo - but only if the copy is verified at the BLOB level. `git hash-object` and `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` both have to match the upstream blob, because a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf warns 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' on the very file whose byte-identity is the contract, and only the blob answers the question.

PowerShell's default text writers are a live hazard for checked-in artefacts on this machine: `Set-Content`/`Out-File` wrote a 8169-byte UTF-8 JSON file as 16772 bytes of UTF-16LE with a BOM, and vite:json refused it. Write bytes explicitly (`[System.IO.File]::WriteAllBytes` with `[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes`) or fetch raw bytes, and check the first bytes after writing.

PowerShell cannot do heredocs. `git commit -F - <<'MSG'` is a parse error; write the message to a file under .git/ and use `git commit -F <file>`. Cost: one wasted command, and a multi-line commit message is otherwise impossible to pass safely.

A re-pointed test is a place a lane can quietly weaken a control: four retired expectations in this lane's own suite would have gone green by being deleted. Re-pointing them (same coverage, plus the half of the new ruling that must not move) is the version that keeps the suite honest, and the mutation proves the re-pointed assertions still fire.

Before writing a divergence test, check whether the equality it asserts can be VACUOUS: if every row pinned the same answer, 'the rule agrees with every row' would pass for any rule. Assert the fixture spans the decision space (both slate answers, every kind, every refusal code, a null form) in the same file.
DEAD_END: Writing the fixture copy with PowerShell's default encoder: 16772 bytes of UTF-16LE+BOM, vite:json 'Failed to parse JSON file'. Fetch raw bytes via `gh api .../contents/<path>?ref=<ref> --jq .content` (base64) and WriteAllBytes instead.
